office_does: A King County West Electoral District District Court judge hears and decides misdemeanor criminal cases, small claims, traffic cases and protection orders for a four-year term; in practice the discretion is in pretrial release, sentencing, protection orders and therapeutic-court supervision.
race_blurb: Judge Bardi Martin, a former public defender unanimously appointed by the County Council in January 2026, faces pro tem judge Nyjat Rose-Akins, a former Seattle city prosecutor and civil city attorney. The race skipped the primary. Martin is endorsed by the King County Democrats and The Stranger; Rose-Akins lists three Supreme Court justices and the Attorney General and has raised about three times as much.

candidates.summary: District Court judge since a unanimous King County Council appointment in January 2026, after about two years pro tem and 18 years of practice that began in public defense. He says he presides over the Shoreline/Kenmore Community Court.
highlights: Appointed 9-0 by the King County Council on Jan. 27, 2026 (Motion 16944) [S2]
Public defender for three years, then managing member of a civil and criminal litigation firm [S3][S5]
Says he presides over the Shoreline/Kenmore Community Court, which links low-level defendants to housing and treatment [S1][S7]
Rated Well Qualified by KCBA and QLaw at appointment (council record) [S4]
Endorsed by the King County Democrats and The Stranger [S10][S11]

safety.basis: Public-defense formation plus a self-reported Community Court role connecting defendants to services; no bail statement.

experience.basis: Sitting judge by merit-selection appointment running on bench experience, though only about nine months in the seat.

candidates.summary: Pro tem judge and court commissioner pro tem who was a Seattle city prosecutor from 2010 to 2016 and then a civil city attorney advising SPD and city departments until 2023.
highlights: Seattle Assistant City Prosecutor 2010-2016, then civil precinct liaison attorney advising SPD until 2023 [S2]
Reports pro tem service setting pretrial release conditions and hearing protection-order and ITA matters [S2]
Washington Women Lawyers rated her Well Qualified; her claimed KCBA rating could not be checked (KCBA's 2026 page omits this race) [S3][S4]
Endorsed by five LD Democratic organizations, three Supreme Court justices and AG Nick Brown, per her statement [S1]
Has raised about $50,200, roughly three times her opponent [S7]

safety.basis: Prosecution formation (six years of misdemeanor prosecution) followed by civil work advising police; no bail position, with some prosecutorial work alongside Mental Health and Community Court participants.

experience.basis: Mixed: 16 years of practice and pro tem service, challenging a recently appointed incumbent.
